title: Social Anxiety Symptoms and Body‐Focused Repetitive Behaviour Severity in Adolescents: A Serial Mediation Analysis of Shame and Emotion Regulation Difficulties
abstract: ABSTRACT Body‐focused repetitive behaviour disorders (BFRBDs), including trichotillomania (TTM) and skin‐picking disorder (SPD), typically emerge during adolescence. These disorders have been conceptualized within emotion regulation models, in which body‐focused repetitive behaviours (BFRBs) may function as attempts to regulate aversive emotional states. Although anxiety frequently co‐occurs with BFRBDs, its association with BFRB severity is generally modest, highlighting the need to examine affective and regulatory processes. This cross‐sectional study examined the associations among social anxiety, shame‐proneness, emotion regulation difficulties and BFRB severity using a serial mediation model. Participants were 107 adolescents aged 12–18 years (80.4% female) who met DSM‐5 criteria for TTM or SPD and were recruited from a tertiary child and adolescent psychiatry clinic. Diagnoses were established using semi‐structured clinical interviews. The analysis controlled for age and sex. Social anxiety was positively correlated with shame, emotion regulation difficulties and BFRB severity ( r = 0.28–0.31, all p < 0.01). In the serial model, social anxiety was associated with greater shame, which was associated with greater emotion regulation difficulties; in turn, emotion regulation difficulties were associated with greater BFRB severity. The total indirect effect ( B = 0.162, 95% CI [0.038, 0.337]) and the serial indirect effect through both mediators ( B = 0.117, 95% CI [0.040, 0.257]) were significant, whereas neither single‐mediator indirect effect was significant. The direct association remained significant ( B = 0.302, p = 0.022), consistent with partial statistical mediation. These findings support the proposed theory‐based model but do not establish temporal or causal ordering.
